# Interpreting the HUMAN_GNLY → CD45RA Attribution Tree in Cord Blood

## 0. What the tree is actually telling us

Class 1 = the top decile of *positive* Integrated Gradients attribution of GNLY toward the CD45RA prediction. Because standard 3′ scRNA-seq cannot resolve the PTPRC exon-A splicing that defines CD45RA, the MLP must infer the CD45RA epitope from **cell identity**. GNLY works as an attribution feature precisely because it is an almost exclusively **NK/cytotoxic-lymphocyte** granule gene, and NK cells are a strongly CD45RA+ (CD45RO−) population in cord blood. The tree's job was to find *in which transcriptomic context* GNLY carries that predictive weight — and the answer is unambiguous:

- **742/860 TP (86% of all Class-1 cells)** sit in the three NK-cytotoxic leaves (Nodes 18/19/20), with **Node 20 (TP 512, Precision 85.6%, Gini 0.077)** the single most robust zone — an ~8.6-fold enrichment over the ~10% class base rate.
- **Node 12 (TP 104, 57.1%)** is the second-largest zone and is biologically distinct (GZMB-low).
- Nodes 6/10 (HOPX/CTSW, ≤3 TP) and Node 11 (22.5% precision) are low-confidence and treated only as background.

---

## 1. PRIMARY ZONE — Node 20 (with sibling Node 19): the CD94-high cytotoxic NK zone

**Logic:** NKG7 > 1.22 ∧ GZMB > 1.42 ∧ CST3 ≤ 0.78 ∧ KLRD1 > 2.15 (thresholds in normalized log space: "high/low expression").

**Narrative:** GNLY's positive contribution to CD45RA prediction is *gated* by an NKG7-permissive cytotoxic context, then *refined* to NK identity by two opposing locks: (i) GZMB + KLRD1 (CD94, the NKG2A partner) confirm the NK arm of the cytotoxic module — critical because GZMB alone is shared with CTLs, and the KLRD1-high gate pushes the zone away from T cells (note the sibling Node 19, KLRD1-low, drops from 85.6% → 74.1% precision); (ii) CST3-low (cystatin C) plus the S100A12-high exclusion branch removes monocyte/granulocyte confounding. The tree therefore recapitulates a compositional logic: **GNLY-high cells in cord blood are NK cells; NK cells are CD45RA-high; hence GNLY positively drives the CD45RA prediction.** The KLRD1 > 2.15 dominance specifically matches neonatal NK biology — the cord blood NK compartment is enriched for CD94/NKG2A-high, KIR-low, cytotoxically immature CD56-bright-leaning cells.

### Category 1 — findings that directly confirm known biology
1. GNLY (granulysin) is a saposin-like effector of NK/CTL cytotoxic granules [3, 4]. ✔
2. NKG7–GZMB–KLRD1 co-expression is the canonical NK signature; CST3 and S100A12 are monocyte/myeloid markers [5, 7, 11]. ✔
3. NK cells express the long CD45 isoform (CD45RA) and lack CD45RO, so GNLY-high cells sit inside the CD45RA-high compartment [1, 2]. ✔
4. Neonatal/cord blood NK cells are CD94/NKG2A-dominant and cytotoxically immature — explaining why the KLRD1-high leaf is the purest [5, 6, 8, 10]. ✔

### Category 2 — new, testable mechanisms
- **H1 (proxy vs. cause):** GNLY is a marker, not a regulator, of CD45RA. *Test:* in-silico ablation of GNLY in the MLP (prediction should collapse in Node-20 cells only) + CRISPRi/siRNA GNLY in primary cord NK (predicted: surface CD45RA unchanged; granule-mediated killing/antimicrobial activity reduced) [3, 15].
- **H2 ("cytotoxic-yet-CD45RA" maturation state):** a KLRD1-hi GZMB+ GNLY+ neonatal NK state retains CD45RA/CD45RO− until adult-like or CMV-like pressure. *Test:* flow panel (CD45RA/RO, CD94/NKG2A, intracellular GNLY/GZMB) on paired cord vs. adult blood; IL-15/IL-12/IL-18 culture time course [5, 6, 8–10].
- **H3 (CST3–cathepsin axis):** within GZMB+ cells, low CST3 (cystatin C) may permit cathepsin C–dependent pro-granzyme maturation, defining the granule-loaded state in which GNLY is also packaged. *Test:* cystatin C knockdown/overexpression in NK-92 or primary NK → measure pro-granzyme processing, GZMB/GNLY granule loading [12, 15].
- **H4 (Node 18 as a QC flag):** the GZMB+ CST3-high leaf (TP 41) plausibly captures NK–monocyte doublets/ambient RNA; the 0.78–0.82 CST3 "no-go band" is a purity boundary, not biology. *Test:* re-run with doublet detection (Scrublet/DoubletFinder).

---

## 2. SECONDARY ZONE — Node 12 (sibling Node 11): the NKG7-high / GZMB-low "pre-granule" zone

**Logic:** NKG7 > 1.22, and within S100A12 ≤ 1.72 (myeloid exclusion), this leaf specifically requires **NKG7 > 1.50 with GZMB ≤ 1.42**.

**Narrative:** Here the model leans on the *broader* cytotoxic module (NKG7) without the mature granule arm (GZMB). Two candidate identities are compatible: (i) **CD56-bright, cytokine-biased NK cells** — CD94-high, GZMB-low, the dominant NK subset in cord blood; or (ii) **NKG7+ T cells** (early-cytotoxic CD8 or rare CD4) — which in cord blood are essentially all naive CD45RA+. In either case these are CD45RA+ cells, so the MLP again converts a cytotoxic-program feature into positive CD45RA evidence, just with lower confidence (57.1%) than the NK-locked primary zone. The graded thresholds are informative: Node 11 (NKG7 1.22–1.50) is noisy (22.5%), so attribution strength scales with NKG7 intensity — a dose-response signature of program onset.

### Category 1 — literature-consistent findings
1. NKG7 is a pan-cytotoxic marker expressed before/alongside effector granule genes [5, 7]. ✔
2. CD56-bright NK are GZMB-low, CD94-high, cytokine-producing — precisely this leaf's gap (NKG7+ GZMB−) [5, 6]. ✔
3. Cord blood lymphocytes are overwhelmingly naive CD45RA+ [9, 10], so any lymphocyte-resolved cytotoxic program still lands in CD45RA+ cells. ✔

### Category 2 — new testable mechanisms
- **H4 (temporal ordering "NKG7-first"):** NKG7 induction precedes GZMB/GNLY granule maturation during NK activation, with CD45RA retained through the transition. *Test:* IL-15 ± IL-18 stimulation time course on cord NK with scRNA + scATAC (NFIL3/PRDM1/ETS1 dynamics) and CD45RA protein tracking [5, 6, 15].
- **H5 (identity resolution):** discriminate CD56-bright NK vs. NKG7+ T cells via CD3D/IL7R/TCF7 vs. NCAM1/KLRC1 co-expression (these were not top-29 IG features, hence invisible to the tree). *Test:* index sorting + CITE-seq; functional CD107a degranulation assay on the NKG7+ fraction.
- **H6 (module-level attribution):** test whether the MLP treats NKG7 as a GNLY-family surrogate by comparing marginal IG of NKG7 vs. GNLY across both zones.

---

## 3. Cross-zone synthesis

| Zone | Logic core | TP | Precision | Interpretation | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **20** (+19) | NKG7+ GZMB+ KLRD1hi CST3lo | 512 (+189) | 85.6% (74.1%) | Mature, CD94-high neonatal NK → CD45RA+ | **Robust (primary)** |
| **12** (+11) | NKG7hi GZMBlo S100A12lo | 104 (+9) | 57.1% (22.5%) | CD56-bright NK / NKG7+ naive T | Plausible (secondary) |
| 18 | GZMB+ CST3hi | 41 | 66.1% | Likely doublets/ambient | QC signal |

**Why GNLY "heavily attributes" to CD45RA:** GNLY is the most NK-specific gene in the feature set; in cord blood the cytotoxic compartment is NK (no adult TEMRA memory-CD8 ambiguity), and NK are CD45RA-high/CD45RO−. The tree shows the attribution is *conditional*: it exists only inside an NKG7+ gate, is maximized in the KLRD1-high, CST3-low mature NK state, and is actively suppressed in myeloid (S100A12/CST3-high) contexts.

## References (verify details before citing; provided from memory)
[1] Stoeckius M, et al. *Nat Methods* 2017 — CITE-seq (cord blood PBMCs; CD45RA/RO ADTs). [2] Trowbridge IS & Thomas ML. *Annu Rev Immunol* 1994 — CD45 isoforms. [3] Stenger S, et al. *Science* 1998 — granulysin-mediated cytotoxic activity. [4] Clayberger C & Krensky AM. *Curr Mol Med* 2003 — granulysin review. [5] Cooper MA, Fehniger TA & Caligiuri MA. *Trends Immunol* 2001 — CD56-bright/dim, CD94/NKG2A. [6] Caligiuri MA. *Blood* 2008 — human NK biology. [7] Monaco G, et al. *Cell Rep* 2019 — NK/myeloid deconvolution signatures (GNLY, NKG7, KLRD1, CST3, S100A12). [8] Levy O. Neonatal innate immunity review, 2007. [9] Adkins B, et al. *Nat Rev Immunol* 2004. [10] Olin A, et al. & Brodin P. *Cell Syst* 2018 — newborn immune development reference. [11] Hofmann MA, et al. *Cell* 1999 — S100A12/EN-RAGE myeloid axis. [15] Trapani JA & Smyth MJ. *Nat Rev Immunol* 2002 — perforin/granzyme cytotoxic pathway.

**Caveats:** IG attribution reflects model reliance, not gene causality; class_weight (1:4) boosts Class-1 recall, so precision in small leaves (Nodes 6/10/11) is unstable; all thresholds are in normalized model space and should be translated back to raw counts before experimental gating.
